summary.answer: The new connection is a phase-aware input map, not another reconstruction of the old damage predicate. Ordinary spawn writes sessionteam=self.team and sessionstate=playing and refreshes spawntime before later on_player_spawned/insertion work. A redeploy batch merely threads the spawnclient route, whose admission/queue branches mean selection is not proof of a fresh spawn clock. Spectator camera/sessionstate and spectator sessionteam are distinct; should_do_player_damage vetoes only the latter. No explicit candocombat writer is present in the 2,632 frozen GSC/CSC references; its effective producer and original value remain unknown. Insertion holds, begin/teleport flags and HMH doublejump/fallheight branches do not directly write those inputs in the cited spans. Spawn protection is the script elapsed<=cached-ms comparison, checked here only with bit 8; equality counts. Native invulnerability is a separate earlier callback veto, with a visible warzonestaging value-registry chain to enable/disableinvulnerability but unresolved native effects and stacked resets. End_round writes postgame before onendround and the table/server-notify/clientfield end channels. Warzone's later game_ended matchflag pulse does not change that state and therefore does not reopen ordinary admission. Finally, ordinary game-over rejection does not erase the earlier postgame hook: allowed trigger-hurt/crush paths may already call finishplayerdamage as MOD_POST_GAME. All remaining old vetoes/returns are reused unchanged; none of these connections proves HMH runtime behavior or closes the native down-versus-kill decision.
